properties.description:
The OAuth 2.1 CLIENT role that req:every-oauth-role-reflow2-plays-meets-oauth-2-1-at-a-minimum named as "LATER", planned 2026-10-01 on Anthony's word ("Plan it now", no code yet).

WHAT IT DOES: `reflow2-mcp setup remote <url>` signs in instead of asking for a pasted key whenever the server says it is a protected resource. The steps:
- Read the 401's WWW-Authenticate.
- Find the protected-resource metadata (RFC 9728), then the authorization server's metadata (RFC 8414 / OIDC, issuer checked).
- Register in the MCP order: pre-registered, then a Client ID Metadata Document, then DCR.
- Open the system browser at an authorization-code request carrying PKCE S256, state and `resource` (RFC 8707).
- Take the code on a one-shot loopback listener, check state and `iss` (RFC 9207), and exchange it.
- Keep the refresh token in the OS keychain beside today's keys.
`--remote`, the pointer attach and the design watch (upstream.rs) then take a token SOURCE that refreshes before expiry. It retries a 401 once after a refresh, never after a timeout, and steps up scope on 403 insufficient_scope.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE: personal keys stay supported and keep working exactly as today. Local use (stdio, --shared, loopback) involves no OAuth. reflow2 still issues no tokens.

The plan, the owner's open choices and the tests to write first are on epoch:planned-reflow2-signs-in-as-an-oauth-client.
properties.name: reflow2's remote client signs in to its server with the browser (OAuth 2.1 authorization code + PKCE), and keeps and refreshes the token in the OS keychain
